style: retail swing/position trader, growth-stock fundamentals plus chart timing
edge_principles: Screen the universe on fundamentals (EPS and revenue growth, return on equity) and use the chart only for timing
Decide the exit (fixed max loss of about 8-10%) and an expected profit target before entering; place the stop immediately
Once price reaches the expected target, tighten the stop sharply so a winner cannot become a loser
Trade with the broad index trend; most stocks follow the market direction
Specialise in a handful of names to learn their recurring intraday and range behaviour
Review every trade on the chart, winners as well as losers
notes: Career/journey interview; mostly general swing-trading process. One loosely specified fundamental-filter swing approach and an anecdotal range trade, no precise intraday rules.

style: retail options premium seller (Option Alpha)
edge_principles: Implied volatility tends to overstate realized moves; be a net seller of options premium
Act like a casino: many small, independent, high-probability bets rather than few large ones
Risk 1-5% of the account per position; a cited tastytrade study showed the same 75% win-rate strategy losing half the account at 50% allocation versus gaining at 5%
Liquidity first: only trade stocks with >1M shares/day and tight option spreads, otherwise the edge is lost in the bid-ask
Check portfolio-level directional balance (net delta) before adding a trade; skip good setups that make the book lopsided
Diversify across expiries and strategies, not just underlyings
Commit to a fixed rule set for ~a year / 100+ trades before judging a high-win-rate strategy
Roll losing short-premium positions out in time for a credit instead of closing
notes: Options-selling philosophy interview; describes short strangles/iron condors in general terms with no precise strike/DTE rules, so no concrete stock setup extracted.

style: retail penny-stock momentum and short seller
edge_principles: Choose a niche with weak competition (low-priced stocks large funds ignore)
Only trade the hottest movers of the day; ignore stocks that are not moving
Cut losses very quickly; one large loss is what ruins small-cap traders
Take the 'meat' of a move (10-30%) rather than trying to catch the top or bottom
After a losing streak, trade smaller, paper trade or stop - do not size up to win it back
notes: Introduces his pump-and-dump short thesis at a high level; no precise trigger, so the single setup is low confidence.

style: systematic end-of-day trend follower and short-term mean reversion (The Chartist)
edge_principles: Know why the strategy makes money so you can tell a regime mismatch from a broken system
Trend following wins ~50% with 3:1 payoffs; accept long flat periods (e.g. 24% in one quarter, nothing for 8 months)
Diversify by adding uncorrelated strategies (trend breakout + short mean reversion) rather than switching after a drawdown
Commissions and small account size can require 20-40%/yr just to break even; size capital to the trade frequency
Measure realized slippage per trade; an illiquid-market strategy lost 11-15%/yr to about $45 slippage per trade
Fixed-fractional sizing: a 10% stock stop equals ~0.5-0.8% of capital when held in a portfolio
Automate end-of-day order generation; no intraday watching
notes: Systematic process interview. Two strategies described at a structural level (ASX small-cap momentum breakout, S&P 500 3-day mean reversion) without exact parameters.

style: retail trend follower / swing trader (New Trader U)
edge_principles: Risk at most 1% of capital per trade and at most ~3% total open risk across positions
Size positions by the instrument's daily range so a full adverse day costs no more than the 1% budget
Use end-of-day (closing) stops when position size is small enough to tolerate intraday noise
Avoid deep drawdowns: a 50% loss needs 100% to recover
Accumulate enough capital before trading actively (he suggests $25-30k) so costs do not dominate
React to price; do not predict
notes: Mostly risk-management and mindset. Gives three concrete daily-chart rules: RSI swing in an uptrend, range breakout to all-time highs with MA trailing stop, and index 200-day reclaim.

style: retail Gann-based swing trader, daily charts
edge_principles: Establish the bigger trend on weekly/monthly charts first; take mainly longs in bull phases and shorts in bear phases
Avoid trading signals in sideways/choppy markets; most whipsaw comes from ignoring regime
Split the position: take half at a high-probability target, hold the other half for an extended move
Add on fresh signals in the trend rather than all at once
Review past trades on the chart; one subscriber found all profits came from three setups in three markets - cut everything else
Specialise in 2-3 markets and no more than two concurrent trades
Range-vs-volume reading: a narrowing range on equal volume signals more supply entering
Treat widely publicised bullish/bearish news near extremes as a contrary signal
notes: Gann-style swing trading on daily charts. Main setup is the 50% retracement coinciding with a double/triple bottom, confirmed by a swing-chart signal.

style: ex-prop tape reader; equity and options (weeklies) day/swing trader
edge_principles: Edge for a discretionary human is reading the tape (Level 2 + time and sales) for large-player accumulation footprints
Never trade in front of a news release; wait for the algorithmic reaction to finish and trade after
Scale out into strength (sell into the move) rather than waiting to exit the whole size at the top - liquidity vanishes at the turn
Swing trading one or two names and waiting for the big move was his most consistent mode; constant day trading led to overtrading
Trading to cover rent or recover losses produces forced trades; stand aside on no-opportunity days
After a run of losses, size down for weeks until a few winners restore confidence
Large size in options is visible to market makers; vary execution and order routing
notes: Mostly career and psychology. His method is discretionary tape reading of accumulation before breakouts, with no measurable rules; one high-discretion setup recorded.

style: hedge fund operator (SangLucci Capital), options premium seller, HFT/market-structure
edge_principles: Measure P&L per share/contract; many break-even hand traders are simply losing the spread they cross - passive (limit) entries can flip them to profitable
Order-flow routing matters: sold/internalised flow gets picked off in fast markets; route directly or use smarter execution
He cites that well under a third (~28%) of intraday breakout attempts succeed; markets chop more than they trend intraday, so be selective with breakouts
Set stops according to the participant timeframe you are trading (swing positions should not carry day-trader-tight stops)
Know your regime: scale up in conditions that suit your style (he sells premium in choppy markets, scales back in breakout markets)
Write entries/exits as explicit if-then pseudocode so entry and exit signals are consistent
Discretionary size does not scale linearly; increase size gradually with emotional tolerance
notes: Market-structure and career interview. No concrete setup; key quantitative claim is that most intraday breakouts fail and spread-crossing explains much of retail break-even P&L.

style: retail small-cap momentum trader, mainly short seller of overextended runners
markets: US OTC and NASDAQ small caps
edge_principles: Use a broker whose execution fits the strategy; slow fills turn a planned small stop into a large loss
Trade only liquid, volatile names (he wants >= ~$5M traded on the day for listed stocks)
Narrow to one or two setups, track each in a spreadsheet (returns, frequency) before sizing up
Trade the ticker, not the company: ignore fundamental bias when price breaks your level
Place stops at chart levels, then size the position so the distance to that level fits the dollar risk
Never average up into a short that breaks to new highs of the run; a $290k loss came from holding and adding
Hiding the open P&L column reduced emotional exits
notes: Small-cap specialist; two daily-chart setups (fading multi-day spikes in listed small caps, buying breakouts to new highs of an OTC promotion) plus buying newly announced promotions (not testable).

style: independent intraday equities trader, VWAP-based, moving to systematic
edge_principles: Use VWAP as the day's honest average price and primary bias filter; it is fast early, slows midday, picks up slightly near the close
Prefer liquid, 'boring' large caps over in-play news names; a 45-cent move in a mega cap is enough
Decide direction first, then location; if odds are strongly one way, enter with partial size instead of waiting for a perfect entry
A setup is only worth trading if it shows positive expectancy across hundreds of stocks, not a few charts
Think in expectancy = payoff x probability, including sizing, partial exits and stop handling - not raw risk:reward
Master one approach deeply before adding others
Keep stakes small early; mental burnout ends more careers than blown accounts
His busiest/most important window is 10:00-12:00 ET
notes: Two-hour VWAP philosophy interview with little precise rule detail; one loosely specified VWAP bias setup recorded.

style: retail futures day trader, market/volume profile and price action (Optic Trading)
edge_principles: Top-down: mark key reference zones on monthly, weekly, daily then 5-min charts before the open
Trade value (where volume accumulates in the profile), not just price; migrating value signals direction
Within a balance area, trade from extremes; the middle is chop
Rest limit orders at pre-planned levels and let the market come to you
Expect 3-5 years to consistency; stay on simulation until profitable there
Add a new market via historical replay, then sim alongside live markets, then small live size
After a stop-out, never double size to win it back (revenge trading caused his largest loss)
notes: Profile-based futures day trader with 11 setups; describes one in detail, the balance-area breakout failure.

style: short-timeframe discretionary price-action trader (YTC), ex-military pilot
markets: CL futures, Russell/Dow e-minis (previously FX, ASX)
edge_principles: Three timeframes: higher (5-min) for support/resistance structure, trading (1-min) for trend, lower (15-sec/range) for timing
Only five trade types: breakout failure, test of S/R, breakout pullback, simple pullback, complex pullback
Metagame: enter where you know others will be forced to buy (or sell) after you - at the point trapped traders give up
Very tight initial stops; scratch quickly if price does not move away immediately, and re-enter if the premise is still valid
After two full losses in the same setup area, stop and wait for a new area
Evaluate performance in groups of ~20 trades (win %, win/loss size ratio, streaks) rather than single trades or lifetime stats
Have other income covering living expenses before going full time
Keep a daily market structure/price action journal of printed charts
notes: Price-action scalper; framework is clear but discretionary. Two setups recorded in MCF-translatable form.

style: fully algorithmic intraday FX trader, trading-software company founder
markets: FX majors (5-6 pairs); formerly Johannesburg stocks
edge_principles: Run several uncorrelated strategy types (trend following and mean reversion) across 5-6 instruments simultaneously
Expect any single intraday strategy to decay within 3-6 months (maybe a year); keep a pipeline of replacements
Flatten before the very highest-impact scheduled events (e.g. Fed chair speeches); trade through ordinary news
Segment instrument behaviour by time of day; ignore low-volatility sessions (he studies EUR/USD only in the London session)
Backtest with event-driven, portfolio-level engines that model realistic time-of-day spreads; judge drawdown on mark-to-market equity, not closed-trade equity
Pay to have an idea coded and backtested before trading it; disproving an idea cheaply is a win
Standard indicator settings are curve-dependent; fixed-parameter RSI/MA strategies rarely hold up
notes: Algorithmic FX trader who explicitly declined to reveal strategies; process and research-hygiene principles only.

style: ex-bank FX strategist turned self-funded contrarian FX swing trader
edge_principles: Treat leverage as the main risk; he suggests trading unleveraged (or <= 5:1) for a full year before scaling
Only take trades you 'love' (A+ conviction), which cuts frequency and regret
Use ATR to judge when the day's move is likely exhausted (price has already covered the average daily range)
Decide once whether you trade through scheduled news and apply it consistently
Keep risk-reward above 1:1
Set price alerts and step away from the screen instead of forcing trades
Write down daily views to curb impulsive trading
notes: Counter-trend FX swing trader; one setup combining multi-timeframe overextension, RSI extremes and ATR-based exits.

style: ex-CBOE floor market maker, options volatility/spread trader
edge_principles: Survival comes from defined risk and position sizing; blowups come from being wrong in a large, levered way, not from being wrong
Cut size when the P&L is down and increase it when up (opposite of the common instinct)
Take a break during a slump; rebuild confidence with small wins
Most annual profit comes in 2-3 months; expect flat and losing stretches
Do not average down losing trades
Unusual option volume (day volume several times open interest, buyer lifting the offer) can precede stock moves
notes: Options market-making veteran. Main idea is unusual-options-activity scanning; one setup (selling inflated calls against stock after an unusual-activity spike) recorded; needs options data.

style: retail swing/trend trader, chart patterns within trends (Leavitt Brothers)
edge_principles: Do not trade in a vacuum: when the index is range-bound, treat every trade as short-term (take 5-10%, no trailing for big moves)
Prefer stocks whose whole industry group is strong; isolated good charts underperform
Classify each trade before entry as quick (days, 4-10% target) or long theme ride (months, loose stop) - mixing the two loses
Add to winners only at higher levels after breakout and rest
Concentrate in 2-3 strong groups; keep only 4-6 short-term positions
Judge yourself by process quality, not trade P&L
Successful floor traders specialised in one narrow edge (e.g. only the first five minutes, or only the jobs report)
Never let a small loss become a big one; avoid style drift and information overload
notes: Daily-chart swing trader; main setup is a consolidation breakout within an uptrend, filtered by market regime and industry-group strength.

style: news/fundamentals-driven day and swing trader, ~60% short bias, biotech specialist
edge_principles: Specialise in one sector (80-90% of trades in biotech) to read news detail faster than the headline
Read the full press release; headlines are often better than the detail
Sell immediately when news or price goes against you, including on a gap - never wait for breakeven
Stop trading for the day after a large unexpected loss; his journal showed attempts to win it back lost more
Use a fixed written rule list and an Excel journal of every trade (size as % of balance, side, P&L)
Move stop to entry once a trade works and let it run
Avoid holding a downtrending biotech into a binary event - the market is often right before the news
notes: News-driven biotech trader with no charts or Level 2; tactics are mostly discretionary. One rule-like setup recorded: avoid/short downtrending biotech into events and exit instantly on a 52-week-high break when short.

style: retail educator; weekly equities and selective FX trend trader
edge_principles: A trading plan must at minimum answer: how do I get in, how much do I risk, how do I get out
Build discipline in small commitments (follow the rule for the next 3 trades) rather than all-at-once resolutions
Be selective: 4-5 FX trades per month rather than taking the best of a bad bunch
Simple rules tested manually bar by bar often work; resist adding complexity
Do not buy every dip in a market that has just changed character (2000 Nasdaq lesson)
Losses become emotionally manageable with exposure and small size
notes: Plan-and-discipline interview; trading approach is generic key-level and trend following in FX, too vague for a concrete setup.

style: momentum day/swing trader, educator (Bulls on Wall Street)
edge_principles: Master one or two go-to setups to microscopic detail rather than knowing many
Stocks with a fresh catalyst (earnings surprise, PR) and high relative volume move independently of the market, so patterns work more cleanly
Hard daily max loss enforced by the platform (his example $2,000); his stats show continuing past it usually deepens the loss
Give-back rule: stop for the day after giving back 50% of the day's peak gains; keep trading while winning on sound setups
'You chase, you die': if you miss the first move, wait for the secondary entries in an in-play stock, including a 14:00-ish afternoon breakout
Learn while employed; needing the money destroys the ability to wait for the right moment
Systematise routines (morning, lunch, close, weekly review) so decisions are pre-made
notes: Momentum trader; main setups are earnings/PR breakouts with strong daily chart, multi-day in-play trading both directions, and an afternoon breakout in hot momentum names.

style: quantitative/discretionary multi-asset swing trader (Waverly Advisors), ex-NYMEX and prop
edge_principles: Real edges are paper-thin; prove them statistically against a random baseline across markets and decades before trusting them
Your eye finds patterns in noise; many popular tools (Fibonacci, Gann, Elliott, MA settings) tested no better than random
Limit risk via small unit size, not artificially tight stops
Being undercapitalised causes many apparent 'psychology' problems; budget ~3-5 years of learning
Stages: first stop losing on trades, then cover costs, only then increase size
Bottom-up breadth: many bullish individual setups in a sector before the sector/index shows it is a real edge
Do not switch timeframes mid-trade (a weekly trade managed off a 5-minute chart, or a scalp held into a big loss)
Strings of wins and losses are normal; judge behaviour consistency, not result consistency
notes: Process and statistics heavy; describes his screening (strong impulse then tight consolidation near highs) rather than full rules. One medium-low confidence setup.

style: prop firm co-founder (SMB Capital), catalyst-driven intraday and swing trader
edge_principles: Many 'psychology' problems are really lack of edge; fix edge first
Trade 'changing fundamentals' names: stocks up/down 3%+ with a news catalyst that changes the story
Name and archive each setup (playbook) with its variables so you can say exactly why a trade is an A+ and size best setups bigger
Risk sizing: swing traders 2-5% per best setup; active intraday traders risk ~30% of the daily stop per trade; always have an intraday stop limit
Beginners: 25% give-back rule on intraday gains
Distinguish fades that revert to the mean from names that trend all day; big losses on trend days wreck a month
Real-time coaching beats education; expect ~8-12 months before progress
Pick a style and timeframe that fits your thinking speed
notes: Two concrete SMB setups: the 'money trade' (catalyst gap-and-go holding above VWAP after price discovery) and the second-day play (break of day-1 key level after earnings). Plus clear sizing/give-back rules.

style: discretionary swing trader turned quantitative multi-system trader (Battle-Fin winner)
markets: US equities (reversion meta-system; intraday ML system in development)
edge_principles: Test entries with naive ('dumb') exits and exits with random entries, separately, keeping organised records
Optimal holding periods in his equity reversion work were shorter than his discretionary instinct expected
Hard stops often sat exactly where mean-reversion edges paid off; small diversified sizing replaced stops in his reversion systems
Run many uncorrelated systems to remove single points of failure
Monte Carlo reshuffling of trade lists reveals likely worst drawdowns (e.g. a 15% historic drawdown can imply ~40% at 95% confidence); size to that
Require many degrees of freedom (trades per rule), statistical significance and consistency across similar stocks
Use survivorship-bias-free, point-in-time index membership when backtesting equities
Monitor live system health (rolling win rate vs expectation) and revert execution changes that diverge from the backtest
Weekly data hides intraweek drawdowns; model risk at the resolution you can suffer it
notes: Quant-process interview; no specific signal rules disclosed (positions small, max <10%, reversionary equity strategy).

style: retail momentum swing trader (3-10 day holds) plus some position trades
edge_principles: Industry momentum is the single biggest factor for short-term winners; focus capital on the hottest groups of the month
Prioritise recent IPOs (first ~6 months, small float) in hot industries
Risk 0.25-1% of capital per trade, scaled by setup and market environment; step aside in corrections
Sell into strength - most swing legs last 3-10 days then consolidate
Study the week's/month's biggest gainers daily and reverse-engineer screens from missed winners
Master one setup with an edge before adding others
Stocks that hold up or build bases during an 8-15% market correction lead the next advance
Partial profits on position trades when weekly RSI > 80; heavy-volume large down day often marks trend end
notes: Clearly specified momentum-continuation swing setup (5>20 MA, consolidation, 2% move to new 20-day high), post-earnings-drift anticipation entries, and correction relative-strength leaders.

style: host's own update: part-time Gann-derived swing trader moving to systematic/automated testing
edge_principles: Start with the minimum account so early mistakes are cheap
Master one subject deeply before moving on, even if you later drop it
A discretionary setup has no known edge until its win rate and payoff are measured across many charts
Prefer simple, discrete rules for a first automated swing system (fewer execution issues than intraday)
Alternate development cycles (research, testing, paper trading) with live trading cycles
notes: Host's progress update; no specific setup rules disclosed beyond a rarely-triggering Gann-derived swing setup.

style: Chicago prop futures day trader, event/news and positioning based
markets: ES (main), European index futures, 10y/30y notes, Euro FX
edge_principles: Biggest trades combine a fundamental 'story' for the day with technical timing; divergences alone are not an edge
Know where other participants are stuck (failed head-and-shoulders, positioning ahead of data) and trade the other way
As order books became algorithm-driven, he enters medium size at chosen areas with wider stops and micromanages less
Review only what you did right or wanted to do (write the ideal trades) rather than dwelling on errors; tag trades by type and search them later
Cut size quickly when a regime changes; his boom-bust cycles came from staying big after conditions changed
Trade the active part of the day, take a midday break, and save energy for volatile periods
Relative-value hedge: long the stronger index future, short the weaker, to sit through noise
notes: Futures event trader; describes a clear failed-news-reaction theme and gap-fill targeting, both translatable to SPY on scheduled-data days.

style: author/analyst (Market Wizards), ex-futures research director, part-time technical trader; FundSeeder co-founder
edge_principles: Money management is essential but cannot rescue a strategy without an edge
Fundamental conviction has no built-in risk control (it says add as price moves against you); technical methods force exits
A failed chart pattern is a stronger signal than a confirmed one
Successful traders adapt: rotate or modify strategies as edges decay with crowding
Seek asymmetric return/risk; flexibility to reverse a view quickly
Apply a moving-average crossover to your own equity curve as a signal to cut size or stop
Ranging-market systems can look great and wipe out in trends - test across regimes
Early failure does not predict long-run outcome
notes: Broad lessons from interviewing top traders; the one testable rule is the classic 'failed pattern' signal.

style: options income (market-neutral index premium selling) plus semi-directional; SMB systems educator
markets: index options (incl. weeklies), stock options, some futures
edge_principles: Replace predictions with several pre-written if-then scenarios per instrument, including what to do when wrong
Frequent-adjustment income strategies on low-priced ETFs lose to commissions; use index options for frequently managed premium trades
Evaluate systems in order: risk (drawdown, capital, loss dispersion), reward, expectancy, return volatility, frequency/costs, trade duration profile, and only last accuracy
Think of each trade as banking the system's expectancy (e.g. $23/trade) rather than a win or loss
Size for the drawdowns history implies are coming (flash crash, 2008, Aug 2011), not last month's results
Trend systems may be 30-40% accurate yet strong; expect clusters of short small losses before long big wins
Willpower and effort that work elsewhere do not work against the market
notes: Options-income trader; one directional setup expressed as explicit if-then plans (pullback-in-trend or held breakout with contracting consolidation).

style: multi-timeframe swing trader (Alphatrends), occasional day trader; VWAP and moving averages
edge_principles: Only price pays: trade price action, treat news as context; avoid holding through earnings (no edge)
Trade only in the direction of the 50-day MA slope; never buy a stock with a declining 50-day
Moving-average levels are reasons to look closer on a lower timeframe, not buy signals by themselves
Moving-average crossovers signal indecision (stage 1/3) - avoid, rather than use as triggers
Read pattern psychology: progressively higher lows and more frequent tests of resistance show buyers getting more aggressive
Don't wait for volume confirmation on breakouts if price triggers; reduce size instead when the market backdrop is weak
Avoid concentrated overnight positions in story stocks
Start on longer horizons; day trading only after swing success
notes: Very concrete multi-timeframe pullback entry (daily trend, 30-min 5-day MA trigger, 10-min alerts) and event-anchored VWAP levels; Weinstein stage analysis framework.

style: systematic long-term trend follower (Trendstat), Market Wizard, retired
edge_principles: Volatility control: per position, 20-day average daily range in dollars / account equity must stay below a set cap; trim positions daily when it is exceeded
Risk control: cap each position's risk to stop as a percent of equity; also cap margin as percent of equity
Uncapped winners can dominate the portfolio (his silver trade); normalise so every market contributes comparably
Trend following ~30% win rate; profits come from a few large trends, so every new position must be treated as the potential big one with a trailing stop that gives room
His random-entry study: with sound exits and sizing, even coin-flip entries can profit - exits and money management matter more than entries
Never change strategy mid-session under stress; review after the close
Start each day assuming you would re-enter every open position; if not, exit
Fully automate execution to avoid daily drudgery and interference
notes: Systematic trend following and sizing framework; main transferable item is the volatility-to-equity sizing rule; entries deliberately de-emphasised.

style: Australian hedge fund / event-driven (takeover arbitrage) and partners' day trading
edge_principles: Seek trades where reward on offer is outsized relative to a known, limited downside; size from the downside, not imagined upside
Compete in niches large institutions ignore (small caps, odd capital-raising and takeover situations)
Know why you make money - randomness can produce profits that are not an edge
Low-market-beta event strategies smooth returns relative to directional trading
Do not abandon stops after a stop-out that would have recovered; plan maximum loss per trade and per series before revisiting
Don't copy elite traders' styles without their resources and edge
notes: Event-driven ASX trader. Setup: buy announced (preferably unconditional) takeover targets near the bid to own a cheap option on a bump/counter-bid. Earlier capital-raising loophole no longer exists.

style: ex-prop (Generic/Carlin) swing trader with intraday 'cash flow' trading; PS60 supply/demand
edge_principles: Turn off the P&L display; trade the setup, not the money
On fast early profits you are holding a 'premium hand' - do not quit at a fixed daily target; press while the tape is good
If the first couple of trades are wrong, stop - losses escalate when you pile on; no revenge trades
Most of the intraday range is set in the first ~3 hours (emotional money); 90% of his day-trading P&L is done by lunch; afternoon is positioning/pinning
Know where overhead supply sits (where emotional buyers meet technical sellers) before buying a breakout; unknown supply causes most breakout rejections
Price action is king: markets that rally on bad news are bullish and vice versa
Learn to make $100/day consistently before targeting more
Slumps: step back, watch order flow, take time off; don't let two red days erase confidence from weeks of good work
notes: Psychology-heavy; PS60 method only described conceptually (supply zones, 60-minute cycle). Two time-of-day setups recorded.

style: UK end-of-day trend-following pullback trader (position holds of months)
edge_principles: Exit the 'beginner's cycle' by stopping constant tinkering and committing to one strategy
Keep a shadow 'discipline' portfolio of trades as the plan dictated; comparing it to the real account shows the cost of discretionary deviations (his was ~400% better)
Review what normal drawdowns look like on your equity curve so pullbacks don't scare you out
A mentor should question your system (where is your stop?) rather than impose theirs
Risking ~2% per trade can compound strongly when the edge is real
Pick the level each stock respects (some respect the 50-day MA, others S/R) for entries and stops
Pyramid: add on each subsequent pullback in a winning trend
notes: End-of-day trend follower buying pullbacks to the stock's respected level (50-day MA or support), cutting quickly on closes below it, adding on later pullbacks.

style: systematic long-term diversified trend-following fund manager (ex-Bear Stearns/JPM analyst)
edge_principles: Diversify across many markets so you can catch whichever trends occur, long or short
Pick a timeframe that fits your psychology; long-term breakout systems have loose entries/exits
Keep stop orders in the market at all times; organise risk per market in a single sheet (position, stop, money at risk)
Proactively face losses instead of 'medicating' them (holding and hoping) - Seykota trading-tribe lesson
Abandoning a system usually reflects poor preparation or lack of commitment to a style
Preparation-heavy systematic trading makes execution simple
notes: Long-term futures trend follower; mentions 200-day breakout entries as the style example. No intraday content.

style: momentum/growth investor (buy high, sell higher), hedge fund manager, StockTwits co-founder, angel investor
edge_principles: Stocks in motion tend to stay in motion; Wall Street keeps paying for growth
Avoid shorting - he finds the math stacked against it; use cash instead
Most of his mistakes are in selling; he scales out on the way up (pyramids out) to match his risk tolerance
Swim in the most liquid names so you can change your mind quickly
Sitting out most of the time leaves attention for the few great pitches
Your first experience with risk shapes your lifelong risk profile; match strategy to it
Use flexible drawdown rules (10-15%) depending on conviction and market strength
notes: Long-horizon momentum investor; one position-trading setup (all-time-high consumer growth brands).

style: classical chartist, futures/FX position-swing trader since 1975 (Factor Trading)
edge_principles: Risk 1% or less of capital per trade with fairly close stops
Win rate ~40%: assume every trade will lose; 10-15% of trades produced ~all net profits
Best trades work immediately and never look back; mentor's rule: never carry a losing position over a weekend (ideally not overnight)
Use closing prices for breakout decisions; intraday probes are noise built to run stops
Prefer horizontal pattern boundaries; diagonal trendlines and symmetrical triangle edges are unreliable
Only 2-4 tradeable patterns per market per year; most charts have no pattern
Cut size and get pickier during losing streaks; keep one plan A instead of switching
Trade identification is overrated versus money management; keep capital first
Fund full-time trading only with capital earned trading, plus 1-2 years of living expenses
notes: Classical chart-pattern breakout trader; concrete rules: horizontal-boundary patterns of >= 8 weeks, daily close breakout trigger, 1% risk, split position management, no trailing stops.

style: ex-SOES scalper and prop owner; ES futures day trader using volume profile and simple statistical edges
edge_principles: An edge is simply a probability of one outcome over another that allows >= 1:1 reward-to-risk; measure it on thousands of days (Excel is enough)
Use statistics to decide which side to press today and size the other side down (e.g. quarter size, small targets)
Wait after the open to see who controls the auction (which side gains more ground per push) and trade with them; if no one controls it, use small targets
Value migrates from one accepted area (high-volume node) to another; failure to hold a new area tends to send price back to the prior point of control
Volume-at-price inside a bar (where the volume occurred vs the close) reveals strength or weakness
Strict daily loss limit; exceeding it means sitting out the next day
Most learning losses pay for behaviour change; make them small and many rather than few and large
Gaps can blow through stops in futures; size for gap risk
notes: Concrete statistical session edges for ES: RTH touches the overnight high or low ~97% of days; after 4 consecutive lower lows a 5th is rare in his data. Plus value-area return-to-POC logic.

style: algorithmic multi-strategy futures trader (World Cup Futures Trading Championship winner), author
edge_principles: Development pipeline: realistic goals -> idea -> walk-forward optimisation with out-of-sample data -> Monte Carlo simulation -> incubation (paper/shelf period) -> live with predefined quit criteria
Keep rules minimal (e.g. one line for entry, one for exit, ~2 optimisable parameters); unease about optimisation means you already overdid it
Re-running 'out-of-sample' tests many times silently turns them in-sample
Incubation weeds out systems that collapse immediately after going live
Trade many uncorrelated strategies (80+) so no single failure is fatal; monthly return std dev fell 3-4x as count grew
Many strategies make it hard to override them discretionarily; override only via preset quit rules
Have enough capital that drawdowns plus living withdrawals don't force decisions
Short option premium blew up 15% in a month (Aug 2015) but diversification kept the month positive
notes: Process-focused algo trader; gives one example of a simple momentum entry (close > close 10 bars ago) to illustrate that simple rules can work.

style: London ex-prop discretionary price-action day/swing trader
edge_principles: Risk/reward evolves during a trade; moving to breakeven when 90 ticks into a 100-tick target means risking 90 to make 10
Don't impose a fixed reward:risk on the market; with a high strike rate 1:1 can be fine - trade level to level
Measure maximum adverse excursion of winners; if winners rarely go 6 ticks against you, a 50-tick stop is far too wide
Keep risk per setup consistent; sizing by gut feel destroys statistics
Trading too large after early windfalls undid good analysis; small size then caused P&L-driven exits - both are P&L trading
Watch for trapped traders at key references; when technicals and sentiment are bearish but price won't fall, look long
Exploiting broker pricing lags is not an edge that lasts
notes: Discretionary trapped-trader trader; two concrete patterns: buying quiet consolidation just under a repeatedly tested resistance (anticipating a probe), and fading the opening gap after an auction failure beyond a reference high/low.

style: ex-CBOE options market maker, later algo options (Trading Machines) and directional options trader
edge_principles: Market makers price options in volatility points and earn the bid-ask edge while staying near delta/vega neutral
Sold or internalised order flow ('exhaust') is picked through by others; be aware of routing
Directional options traders should start by buying defined-risk options and understand capital at risk
When short options and the market moves against you, exit quickly - keep risk tight as market makers do
Low realised volatility shrinks market-maker opportunity
notes: Floor-trading and options-volatility background interview. Mentions buying cheap Friday options on retrace/continuation and possible ~14:00-14:30 buying after a selloff levels off, too vague for a setup record.

style: London ex-prop intraday futures trader using auction market theory / volume profile, NLP and meditation
markets: index and interest-rate futures (started on mini-Dow), spot FX swing
edge_principles: Financial capacity for size is not psychological capacity; oversizing at a prop firm caused intolerable P&L swings
Pick one style (scalper vs longer-intraday) and use matching execution, risk and targets - mixing scalper stops with swing targets fails
Be very selective: one or two good intraday trades per day
Use a risk desk/limits (prop clearing) as an external risk control
Reframe drawdowns as normal costs of business; watch body language cues for overtrading
Don't sell below value or buy above value in balanced conditions
notes: Value-area trader (trade back toward multi-day value; avoid selling below / buying above value). Discretionary; one setup recorded.

style: machine-learning (genetic programming/grammatical evolution) intraday system trader
markets: index futures, FX futures, equities (e.g. AAPL)
edge_principles: Prefer evolved rule-based systems you can read over opaque coefficient models
Only trade systems that worked on all available data; some intraday edges persist ~30 years without re-optimisation
Validate across related instruments (a currency system checked on other currencies) with few parameters (< 5)
Robustness over performance: combine several decent, uncorrelated systems rather than one optimised one
Minimise time in market: 90% cash by each close, flat by Friday, limit orders only - reduces tail-event exposure
Balance portfolio risk (e.g. long-only AAPL systems vs short-only index systems)
Global risk gauges (A/D divergence, VIX new highs, VIX front-month spread) to scale long exposure
Pick new markets that diversify existing exposure, starting with the most liquid
notes: Process for ML-generated intraday systems; signals not disclosed beyond 'price, pattern, seasonality and intraday highs/lows at specific times'.

style: ex-institutional (buy side, sell side, prop) long-only stock trend follower
edge_principles: Risk a fixed 0.5% of capital per position; position size set by distance to the price-based stop
Act on signals immediately; waiting for a pullback that never comes (or limit orders that never fill) costs more than slippage
Use price alone for entry, exit and sizing; fundamentals may help choose between signals but never justify holding a loser ('trade stocks, not companies')
Long only: shorting stocks has asymmetric risk, squeezes, borrow problems; go to cash in bear markets
After long bear markets, new 50-day / 52-week highs from big bases are the first re-entry signals; probe with a few positions
Exits determine win/loss, position size determines by how much, entries only determine frequency
Concentrated portfolio of ~12-15 positions in strong trends
Small accounts face cost drag; costs as a % of risk matter
notes: Long-only new-high trend follower with 0.5% risk per trade.

style: retail technical swing trader with some news-driven day trades
markets: US stocks (all caps incl. low float), ETFs
edge_principles: Never hold swing positions through earnings or known news events; size overnight positions so a gap is survivable
Use ETFs for swing exposure if single-stock gap risk is too much
Start on the daily chart, drill to 60-min (and 15-min) for entries
Price and volume first; indicators only confirm (daily 200 SMA and 50 EMA; intraday 50-period EMA and slow stochastics)
In choppy markets book swing profits faster and shorten holds
Keep charts simple; too many indicators caused paralysis
Early windfall (40k to ~100k in 6 months) led to overconfidence and giving it all back - plan and loss acceptance fixed it (3-4 years to consistency)
notes: Two concrete swing setups: daily chart patterns (flags, ascending/descending triangles, ranges) breaking on volume with measured-move targets, and her favourite 60-minute 50-EMA trend-change pattern.

style: global macro discretionary/systematic hybrid (Mercenary Trader); poker player
edge_principles: Think in positive-expectation bets, not predictions (poker framing: would this action make money over 1,000 repeats?)
Profits are fat-tailed (~90% from ~10% of trades): trade small most of the time and press hard (size varying up to 40-50x) when conditions align
Big-bet checklist: alignment across related markets, clarity of the thesis, resonance of all factors, and flowing (trending) price action
Pyramid into winners as the trade develops
Form macro themes/scenarios, then require price confirmation before entering
Watch macro relationships (e.g. strong dollar is bearish for commodities)
Use systematic rules for position management even when entry decisions are discretionary
Stop behaviours with negative return on effort
notes: Macro trader; example short energy stocks after Nov-2014 OPEC no-cut confirmed by chart breakdowns. Mostly sizing/edge philosophy; no intraday setup.

style: opening-session reversal day trader using short-dated options on volatile stocks; manages client money
markets: US tech and biotech stocks via options
edge_principles: Quality over quantity: 1-3 trades per day, done by ~10:15-10:30 ET
Most of the day's extremes are set in the first 30 minutes; trade the open, then stop
Commissions punish high trade counts
Exit at a fixed risk tolerance (he uses 2%) and trail winners in small increments
Revenge trading after one loss is how both of his blown accounts happened
Managing others' money reduced his emotional attachment and improved execution
notes: Concrete opening-gap exhaustion reversal (fade gap extension on fading volume / buy capitulation at support) in volatile names during the first 30 minutes.

style: penny-stock momentum trader/short seller and large retail educator (Profit.ly)
edge_principles: Track every setup in spreadsheets (e.g. performance on day 1/2/3 of a promotion), as his top student Grittani does
Profits are concentrated: a student made ~80% of profits from ~6% of trades - focus on fewer, better trades
Avoid scalping with oversized positions; one or two oversized losers wipe out accounts
Be transparent/accountable about trades with a community to improve
Short-seller impatience cuts losses well but also cuts winners short (his biggest days would have doubled with another hour)
Small-cap strategies have limited scalability (borrow, liquidity)
A big divergence between promotional press releases and SEC filings flags pump-and-dump shorts
notes: Motivation/education-business interview; restates his two core plays (short pump-and-dumps, buy earnings winners) without new rule detail. One low-confidence long setup recorded; the short is covered in ep003.

style: Market Wizard; discretionary futures swing/day trader guided by simple statistical price models
markets: futures (index, rates, commodities); formerly equity options
edge_principles: Build simple models by asking one question of price (e.g. what follows two up days?) with one or two filters - robust, but a bias not a bet-the-farm signal
Prepare the game plan the night before from models; adjust for overnight action
Probe with the bias: advance when price yields, back off when it resists
Trade location matters in ranges (only at the edges; the middle is noise) but not in breakouts/trends - get in, pullbacks may not come
Holding horizon should follow volatility: day trade aggressively in high volatility, hold longer in contracted ranges
~80% of profits come from ~10% of trades/days; stay in the game until the opening appears
Use price-based functions (ATR) in quantitative work rather than oscillator derivatives; her only oscillator is the 3-10 MA oscillator as support
Check liquidity (exit ability) before trading a new market
Build a library of 20+ printed examples of one setup and keep your own replication statistics
Mechanical volatility-breakout system as a 'reset' after drawdowns - small positive expectancy, not a living
notes: Clear statistical-bias framework; three setups recorded: day-3 fade after two low-to-high days inside a range, range-edge trading after a large expansion, and a volatility breakout used as a discipline tool.
